page.overview:
Who is Madam Rosmerta?

Madam Rosmerta (fl. 1970s–2010s) was a British witch who was the landlady of the Three Broomsticks Inn pub in the village of Hogsmeade. Rosmerta was put under the Imperius Curse, cast by Draco Malfoy in 1996. After being placed under the curse, she helped Malfoy against her will to smuggle cursed items into Hogwarts Castle. It is likely she later redeemed herself by fighting in the Battle of Hogwarts.

Rosmerta was born into a family of unknown wizarding descent no later than 1955 and attended Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry during her formative years.

By the 1973–1974 school year, Rosmerta had graduated from Hogwarts and worked as the barmaid at the Three Broomsticks in Hogsmeade, during which time the establishment would be visited by the Marauders whilst they were all still at school, and continued to do so throughout the First Wizarding War. During the conflict, the young Rosmerta, despite living in constant fear of the prospect that the worst of wizardkind would emerge victorious, nevertheless played a small role in passing on useful information she overheard at the inn, though she mostly just kept her head down. Like most of the magical community, she also suffered personal bereavements during the first period of Voldemort's power, as she knew some of the people who went mysteriously missing,

She also suffered adverse effects from the war herself, as she was one of the numerous witches and wizards who fell victim to what, unbeknownst to herself, were the Frequensting-curse of the Death Eater Antoine Grimalkin, a which inflicted an intensifying, rhythmic stinging pain in its victim along with the echoed looping piece of music from a cursed gramophone, which continued to torment them and even after the sound. Rosmerta was able to deduce it was connected to the Dark Lord and his followers when, on 1 November 1981, she and the rest of his victims, woke up to the news of the Voldemort's defeat and James and Lily Potter's deaths, and the realisation that the mysterious ailment no longer plagued them. She was later one of the many people who believed the rumours that Sirius Black had turned his friends over to Lord Voldemort, and later that he had duelled and killed Peter Pettigrew.
